unit_index.unit_title: Completed L-functions share reflection symmetry
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: The bridge is from a raw L-function to a completed function by adjoining powers of π and conductor and gamma factors, after which s and 1-s become directly comparable.
unit_index.interpretation: Completion exposes a common reflection symmetry while retaining family-specific local data at infinity; the shared form is a structural comparison, not an identification of the functions.

unit_index.source_title: The Riemann Hypothesis
unit_index.unit_title: Removing oldforms isolates primitive newforms with Euler products
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Decomposes the cusp-form space by provenance and distinguishes measuring the new component from constructing its basis; it also identifies what the newform representation gains without importing stronger irreducibility or factorization claims.
unit_index.interpretation: At level q, the new subspace is understood by separating forms generated through two explicit lower-level inheritance mechanisms: level inclusion and dilation f(z)↦f(dz). The source then assigns the newspace a Hecke basis whose elements have associated normalized Euler products and functional equations. This isolates level-new structure, but the dimension formula only measures the subspace; it does not construct the basis, define a quotient, prove categorical irreducibility, or state a factorization theorem for L-functions.

unit_index.source_title: The Riemann Hypothesis
unit_index.unit_title: Vertical zero questions are modeled by random-matrix statistics
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Random-matrix eigenvalue statistics are offered as a comparison representation for vertical zero statistics.
unit_index.interpretation: A pointwise geometric conjecture and a distributional model retain different information: the latter seeks laws of interaction among heights rather than certifying their real parts.

unit_index.source_title: The Riemann Hypothesis
unit_index.unit_title: Cyclotomic-product height bounds encode zeta zero-free half-planes
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Identifies the scalarization step from a polynomial product to averaged boundary size and shows both what analytic region it is claimed to detect and what missing quantifier blocks an automatic RH specialization.
unit_index.interpretation: The defined finite product of cyclotomic polynomials is mapped to a scalar by averaging log-positive magnitude on the unit circle, and the source states an equivalence between a λ+ε growth bound for that height and exclusion of zeta zeros from Re z≥λ+ε. Thus a boundary-growth observable is used as a probe of a zero-free half-plane. The span does not supply the quantification over λ and ε needed to connect this general displayed statement to its opening label as an RH equivalence.

unit_index.source_title: The Riemann Hypothesis
unit_index.unit_title: Growth of an entire series built from reciprocal zeta values characterizes RH
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: The bridge object is the Riesz series, mapping discrete samples 1/ζ(2k) to asymptotic growth in x.
unit_index.interpretation: The factorially weighted generating series compresses reciprocal zeta values at even integers into a global growth observable. Cancellation across its coefficients, not any one coefficient, must enforce the critical exponent.

unit_index.source_title: The Riemann Hypothesis
unit_index.unit_title: Splitting the idele sequence converts inner symmetry into the Bost-Connes outer action
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Covariant representations, the universal crossed product, its generators and relations, and the positive section I+ are the bridge from the finite-adele transfer action to the Bost–Connes symmetry structure.
unit_index.interpretation: The universal property packages every compatible representation of the additive algebra and multiplicative semigroup. Choosing a splitting removes the unit implementers from the restricted algebra, changing the same arithmetic symmetry from inner redundancy to observable outer action.

unit_index.source_title: A strengthening of the Nyman-Beurling criterion for the Riemann hypothesis
unit_index.unit_title: Replacing continuous dilation freedom by natural dilations
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: The bridge is from zeta nonvanishing to Hilbert-space closure, with fractional-part dilates as generators and the characteristic function χ as the target. Restricting the dilation parameter from a real continuum to natural indices exposes an arithmetic subspace inside the original analytic one.
unit_index.interpretation: This is a discretization of an approximation criterion at the level of closed span: a much smaller generating family is asserted to retain the target membership that matters. The strength lies in sufficiency of the discrete generating skeleton, not merely in a change of notation.

unit_index.source_title: A strengthening of the Nyman-Beurling criterion for the Riemann hypothesis
unit_index.unit_title: An epsilon-weighted Möbius family as a reciprocal-zeta correction
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Interprets the exponent as a regularization coordinate and separates analytic representability from topological convergence, showing why the two limits cannot discharge each other's proof obligation.
unit_index.interpretation: Weighting the Möbius coefficients by a complex power creates a family f_s whose fixed-x description is a reciprocal-zeta term minus a spatially finite correction. This gains meromorphic dependence on s as an analytic handle, but it does not by itself give Hilbert-norm convergence or membership in B_nat. The proof architecture therefore assigns different burdens to two stages: under RH, establish f_ε ∈ B_nat for small ε>0; then, unconditionally, prove f_ε → −χ in H as ε↓0.

unit_index.interpretation: The functional equation acts as a symmetry-based change of viewpoint: a difficult zeta ratio is represented by gamma factors whose vertical growth is directly controllable. This isolates a hypothesis-free analytic component of the proof.

unit_index.interpretation: This representation change exposes multiplicative structure hidden in x-space while preserving exactly the norm that controls closure. It converts Hilbert convergence into domination of explicit analytic factors rather than direct manipulation of oscillatory fractional-part sums.

unit_index.source_title: A strengthening of the Nyman-Beurling criterion for the Riemann hypothesis
unit_index.unit_title: The unconditional outer limit closes the strengthened criterion

unit_index.interpretation: The outer limit is logically modular: conditional work supplies membership of each f_ε in B_nat, but the convergence mechanism from that family to the target is hypothesis-free. Norm convergence plus pointwise identification prevents an unspecified closure limit from replacing χ.

unit_index.unit_title: Summability, subsequence criteria, and a possible rate-sensitive refinement

unit_index.interpretation: The source reclassifies the ε-weighted construction as a summability method for the old natural approximation and treats n and ε as truncation and summability coordinates whose special subsequences still give a necessary-and-sufficient convergence criterion. This gains flexibility for comparing summation procedures, but none of those alternatives is analyzed. The unused n-dependence in Lemma 2.1 is only suggested as possibly bearing on the slowness indicated in (1.2); retaining it may motivate rate-sensitive analysis, but no quantitative implication is derived.

unit_index.unit_title: Remote-tail bound for the triangular residual

unit_index.unit_title: Function spaces, dilation spans, and Mellin coordinates for the closure problem
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: The interpretation separates operator availability under all positive scales from the restricted integer-generated algebraic hull, and separates that hull from the stronger integrability gate for analytic Mellin coordinates. This identifies exactly what later reasoning may use and what remains unproved.

B(g) records finite linear reach from g using only the positive-integer dilations K_n, even though K_lambda is available and bounded for every positive lambda; separately, Mellin analyticity on 0<Re(s)<1 is asserted only under membership in every Lp with 1<p<infinity. Thus the definitions supply compatible function-space, dilation-hull, and analytic vocabulary, but this span neither closes B(g) nor proves any transform law connecting dilation to the Mellin variable.

unit_index.source_title: A general strong Nyman-Beurling criterion for the Riemann hypothesis
unit_index.unit_title: Mean cancellation and compact support convert L2 closure into pointwise Mellin vanishing
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: The interpretation identifies mean cancellation as the step that converts an unbounded-domain evaluation problem into a bounded-support continuity argument, and verifies the final algebraic gate: since |2^(1-s)|=2^(1-Re(s))>1 in the stated strip, 1-2^(1-s) cannot vanish.
unit_index.interpretation: The operator V=I-2K_2 does not create compact support: it preserves the compact support already assumed for f while enforcing zero mean. That cancellation makes P F vanish past a bound, and integer dilations of P F share a usable cutoff, so Mellin evaluation of the transformed approximants becomes a bounded-interval L2-continuous functional. Muntz's formula supplies zero Mellin values at the fixed zeta zero, Cauchy-Schwarz passes the zero to F, and the reported factor 1-2^(1-s) is nonzero for 1/2<Re(s)<1, allowing the conclusion f-hat(s)=0. The mechanism proves zero-set inclusion, not RH without a separate nonvanishing hypothesis for f-hat.

unit_index.unit_title: Where the imprimitive extension generalizes and where Speiser correspondence fails

unit_index.interpretation: The passage marks a scope boundary for a Speiser-equivalence proof template: the authors claim that the proof of Theorem 1.6 survives passage to an extended-Selberg zeta-function multiplied by some simple function, whereas for Hurwitz and Lerch zeta-functions they report both the absence of a Riemann-type functional equation and computational nonconfirmation of the Speiser equivalent. This supports treating the positive result as stability under some controlled multiplicative modifications, but it does not establish that the missing functional equation causes the contrasting behavior or that every Speiser-type statement fails in the Hurwitz and Lerch settings. The proof burden left outside the span is to specify the admissible simple factors and hypotheses, supply the Levinson-Montgomery argument, and document what the negative computations test.

unit_index.interpretation: The span defines theta(x) as the sum of the natural logarithms of primes q <= x. Exponentiating gives exp(theta(x)) = product_{q <= x} q, so theta converts the multiplicative contribution of the cutoff primes into one additive scalar. This compression makes the full cutoff product accessible through a sum, but it does not retain each prime contribution as a separately addressable component. The definition alone supplies no estimate for theta, convergence statement, or implication about RH.

unit_index.source_title: On Nicolas Criterion for the Riemann Hypothesis
unit_index.unit_title: Euler product at two and a tail-product upper bound
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Factor the infinite Euler product into cutoff and tail pieces and propagate the explicit tail envelope to derive a quantified finite-product inequality.
unit_index.interpretation: Proposition 1.1 identifies zeta(2) = pi^2/6 with the Euler product of q^2/(q^2-1) over all primes, and Proposition 1.2 bounds the product of the factors with q > x by exp(2/x) for x >= 3. Splitting the full product at x therefore yields zeta(2) <= exp(2/x) product_{q <= x} q^2/(q^2-1). The mechanism replaces an infinite product by a finite prime product with explicit multiplicative slack; it loses the exact tail value and supplies no further conclusion beyond this comparison. Both propositions are cited rather than proved in the span.

unit_index.source_title: On Nicolas Criterion for the Riemann Hypothesis
unit_index.unit_title: Nicolas inequality as an RH equivalence
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Expose the quantifier-preserving reformulation from RH to a family of cutoff comparisons and analyze why sampling cutoffs or converting unconditionally to a ratio would change the claim.
unit_index.interpretation: Nicolas(x) is the strict direct comparison product_{q <= x} q/(q-1) > exp(gamma) log theta(x), and Proposition 1.3 states that Nicolas(x) holds for every x >= 2 if and only if RH is true. The conceptual move is an exact reformulation of one global assertion as a universally quantified family of finite prime-cutoff inequalities. This gains a concrete arithmetic test at each cutoff, but checking selected cutoffs cannot replace the universal quantifier and the criterion does not establish that any required inequality holds. Because theta is not defined in this span, the criterion also depends on the preceding local setup.

unit_index.source_title: On Nicolas Criterion for the Riemann Hypothesis
unit_index.unit_title: Dedekind-psi normalization along primorial products
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Substitute the squarefree cutoff product M_x into the divisor-based definition of Psi, simplify its prime support exactly, and analyze what the subsequent normalization and limit preserve and fail to control.
unit_index.interpretation: The span defines Psi(n) = n product_{q | n}(1+1/q), the primorial-type cutoff M_x = product_{q <= x} q, and R(n) = Psi(n)/(n log log n) for n >= 3, then states unconditionally that R(M_x) tends to exp(gamma)/zeta(2). Since M_x is squarefree and has exactly the primes q <= x as divisors, Psi(M_x)/M_x = product_{q <= x}(1+1/q), so substitution into R turns the cutoff-prime representation into a normalized quantity with a stable displayed limit. The normalization removes the explicit n factor and scales the remaining product by log log n. The limit gives neither a convergence rate nor the side of approach, so it cannot alone justify an eventual one-sided inequality when combined with another vanishing error.

unit_index.source_title: On Nicolas Criterion for the Riemann Hypothesis

unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Take logarithms of the proposed exponential ceiling and compare its eventual universal bound with the cited arbitrarily late strict lower witnesses, isolating the contradiction in their quantifier structure.
unit_index.interpretation: The span defines f(x) = exp(gamma) log theta(x) product_{q <= x}(1-1/q) and claims that RH follows if exp(2/sqrt(x)) >= f(x) for every sufficiently large x. Its proof mechanism is contrapositive: under false RH, a cited Omega-plus premise is expanded into arbitrarily late positive lower-bound witnesses for log f, which eventually exceed 2/sqrt(x); taking logarithms of the proposed envelope instead imposes log f(x) <= 2/sqrt(x) at every sufficiently large input. These quantifiers are incompatible. Packaging the factors into f and moving to logarithms puts the pointwise ceiling and positive spikes on one additive scale, but the lemma remains only sufficient: it does not establish the envelope and depends on the cited Omega-plus result. The OCR-damaged exponent and threshold are not normalized here.

But matching limit constants is weaker than an eventual inequality at their product boundary.
